relevance_reason: This is a review of all congenital myasthenic syndromes. It has a section on rapsyn (RAPSN) deficiency, which is the CMS11 subject, covering clinical features, endplate pathology, the common N88K mutation, the c.-38A>G E-box genotype-phenotype correlation, treatment, and frequency in the Mayo cohort.

findings.statement: In their review, Engel et al. (2015) stated that most patients with CMS due to rapsyn deficiency present in the first year of life and a few present later. Nearly one-third have arthrogryposis at birth and other congenital malformations. Intercurrent infections or fever can trigger respiratory crises leading to anoxic encephalopathy. The clinical features can suggest autoimmune myasthenia gravis, but the ocular ductions are intact in most patients.
quotes: Most patients present in the first year and a few in later life. Arthrogryposis at birth and other congenital malformations occur in nearly one-third of the patients.

Intercurrent infections or fever can trigger respiratory crises resulting in anoxic encephalopathy. The clinical features can suggest autoimmune myasthenia gravis but the ocular ductions are intact in most patients.

phenotypes.text: onset in first year of life
respiratory crises triggered by infection or fever

findings.statement: Engel et al. (2015) reported that in rapsyn deficiency, multiple synaptic contacts appear on single muscle fibers. The endplate AChR deficiency is milder than in primary AChR deficiency, and the junctional folds are poorly differentiated. Different RAPSN mutations hinder rapsyn self-association or binding to AChR, impede agrin-MuSK-LRP4-mediated clustering of AChR, or decrease rapsyn expression.
quotes: Multiple synaptic contacts appear on single muscle fibers (figure 10B). The EP AChR deficiency is milder than in primary AChR deficiency and the junctional folds are not well differentiated (figure 10C and D).
Different mutations hinder rapsyn self-association or binding to AChR, impede agrin-MuSK-LRP4-mediated clustering of AChR, or decrease rapsyn expression.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormal synaptic transmission at the neuromuscular junction

findings.statement: Engel et al. (2015) summarized that rapsyn concentrates and anchors AChR in the postsynaptic membrane and is required for development of the junctional folds. They described its domains: a myristoylated N-terminal region that links it to the membrane; 7 tetratricopeptide repeats needed for self-aggregation and MuSK binding; a coiled-coil domain that interacts with AChR subunits; and a C-terminal domain that binds beta-dystroglycan.
quotes: Rapsyn concentrates and anchors AChR in the postsynaptic membrane and is required for development of the junctional folds.
7 tetratricopeptide repeats are important for rapsyn self-aggregation and to bind to the cytoplasmic domain of MuSK; a coiled-coil domain interacts with long-cytoplasmic loops of AChR subunits

findings.statement: Engel et al. (2015) noted that Indo-Europeans carry a common N88K mutation in RAPSN. Other mutations occur in the promoter region and throughout the RAPSN open reading frame.
quotes: Indo-Europeans harbor a common N88K mutation in RAPSN. Other mutations appear in the promoter region and in the entire open reading frame of RAPSN.

findings.statement: Engel et al. (2015) stated that rapsyn deficiency shows no genotype-phenotype correlations, with one exception. Near-Eastern Jewish patients homozygous for the E-box mutation c.-38A>G have a mild phenotype with ptosis, prognathism, severe masticatory and facial muscle weakness, and hypernasal speech.
quotes: There are no genotype-phenotype correlations except that Near-Eastern Jewish patients with a homozygous E-box mutation (c.-38A>G) have a mild phenotype with ptosis, prognathism, severe masticatory and facial muscle weakness, and hypernasal speech.

findings.statement: Engel et al. (2015) reported that most patients with rapsyn deficiency respond well to AChE inhibitors. Some get additional benefit from 3,4-diaminopyridine, and some from adding ephedrine or albuterol.
quotes: Most patients respond well to AChE inhibitors; some derive additional benefit from 3,4-DAP, and some benefit from the added use of ephedrine or albuterol.
Rapsyn deficiency | Pyridostigmine, 3,4-DAP, albuterol |

findings.statement: Engel et al. (2015) classified 356 index patients with CMS investigated at the Mayo Clinic between 1988 and 2014. Rapsyn deficiency accounted for 51 index cases (14.3%).
quotes: Rapsyn deficiency | 51 | 14.3
Classification based on cohort of congenital myasthenic syndrome patients investigated at the Mayo Clinic between 1988 and 2014

findings.statement: Engel et al. (2015) listed phenotypic clues pointing to rapsyn deficiency: congenital contractures, and sudden apneic episodes provoked by fever or stress. They added that apneic episodes also occur with ChAT mutations and Na-channel myasthenia, and that limb-girdle and axial weakness is occasionally seen with rapsyn mutations.
quotes: Congenital contractures: Rapsyn, AChR δ or γ subunit, ChAT
Sudden apneic episodes provoked by fever or stress: ChAT, Rapsyn, Na channel myasthenia
However, apneic episodes also can occur in patients with Na-channel myasthenia or with mutations in rapsyn.

phenotypes.text: sudden apneic episodes provoked by fever or stress
phenotypes.hpo_label: Apneic episodes precipitated by illness, fatigue, stress

relevance_reason: Case report of a patient with rapsyn deficiency CMS diagnosed by exome sequencing, with treatment response to pyridostigmine.

findings.statement: Das et al. (2014) reported a 20-month-old boy with rapsyn deficiency who presented at birth with weak cry, hypotonia, joint contractures, and facial deformity. Because of respiratory difficulty associated with muscle fatigue, he spent 71 days in the neonatal intensive care unit and 47 days in the pediatric intensive care unit. Imaging, metabolic tests, and electrodiagnostic studies were normal, and muscle biopsy showed myofiber atrophy in a pattern consistent with early denervation.
quotes: We report a 20-month-old boy with rapsyn deficiency. At birth, he presented with a weak cry, hypotonia, joint contractures, and facial deformity.
Because of respiratory difficulty associated with muscle fatigue, he spent a total of 71 days in the neonatal intensive care unit and 47 days in the pediatric intensive care unit.
A muscle biopsy demonstrated myofiber atrophy in a pattern consistent with early denervation.

phenotypes.text: myofiber atrophy consistent with early denervation

findings.statement: In a boy with congenital myasthenic syndrome in whom extensive testing, including microarray, was nondiagnostic, Das et al. (2014) identified 2 pathogenic mutations in the RAPSN gene by whole-exome sequencing.
quotes: Based on nonspecific and nondiagnostic results, whole-exome (next generation) sequencing was performed. This study identified two confirmed pathogenic mutations in the RAPSN gene that are associated with congenital myasthenic syndrome (OMIM 608931).

findings.statement: Das et al. (2014) treated their patient with RAPSN-related congenital myasthenic syndrome with pyridostigmine at 16 months of age, resulting in dramatic improvement in muscle tone and strength and steady resolution of joint contractures; 4 months later he was beginning to bear weight, could sit unsupported, and vocalized full words.
quotes: The patient was treated with pyridostigmine at 16 months of age, which resulted in a dramatic improvement in muscle tone and strength and a steady resolution of joint contractures.
Four months after treatment was initiated, he was beginning to bear weight and was able to sit unsupported and vocalize full words.

relevance_reason: The abstract reports CMS patients with RAPSN mutations, including three new multiexon RAPSN deletions that direct sequencing missed. RAPSN-related CMS with AChR deficiency is the subject of this entry.

findings.statement: Gaudon et al. (2010) described 3 patients who had a typical recessive congenital myasthenic syndrome phenotype and mutations in the RAPSN gene. Family analysis showed that direct sequencing had missed one mutant allele in each patient. Allelic quantification of the patients' DNA found 3 novel multiexon deletions in RAPSN.
quotes: We described here three patients with a characteristic phenotype of recessive CMS and presenting mutation in the gene encoding rapsyn (RAPSN).
Familial analysis showed that one allelic mutation failed to be detected by direct sequencing.
An allelic quantification on patient's DNA identified three novel multi-exon deletions of RAPSN.

findings.statement: Gaudon et al. (2010) found that the 3 genomic rearrangements accounted for 15% of their CMS patients with RAPSN mutations. They emphasized that SNP markers and a gene dosage method should be used alongside direct DNA sequencing, particularly when genetic counseling is at issue.
quotes: These three genomic rearrangements in RAPSN represent 15% of our CMS patients with RAPSN mutations
single-nucleotide polymorphism markers and a gene dosage method should be performed in addition to DNA direct sequencing analysis particularly when there is a genetic counselling issue

relevance_reason: Title reports a founder origin for the common RAPSN N88K mutation that causes congenital myasthenic syndrome with acetylcholine receptor deficiency. This is population-genetic evidence relevant to CMS11.

findings.statement: Müller et al. (2004) concluded that the congenital myasthenic syndrome mutation RAPSN N88K derives from an ancient Indo-European founder.
quotes: The congenital myasthenic syndrome mutation RAPSN N88K derives from an ancient Indo-European founder.

relevance_reason: Haplotype study supporting a founder effect for the rapsyn N88K mutation in CMS with AChR deficiency; also notes asymptomatic homozygotes.

findings.statement: Dunne and Maselli (2004) used 7 intragenic SNPs spanning 8 kb of the rapsyn (RAPSN) gene to characterize the haplotype associated with the N88K mutation. They found a common haplotype in 3 affected N88K homozygotes that was present in all heterozygous carriers of N88K, and concluded that this supported a founder effect.
quotes: we used seven intragenic single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) spanning 8 kb to characterize the haplotype associated with N88K
In three affected N88K homozygous individuals, we identified a common haplotype present in all heterozygous carriers of N88K.
Our findings of a common haplotype associated with the N88K mutation support a founder effect.

findings.statement: Dunne and Maselli (2004) found 2 asymptomatic individuals homozygous for the rapsyn N88K mutation who carried a second haplotype that differed at 3 SNP sites downstream of the mutation. The authors suggested that recombination events may have occurred within the rapsyn gene and that this may have implications for the phenotypic expression of the disease.
quotes: Of note, in two asymptomatic N88K homozygous individuals, a second haplotype was present that differed at three SNP sites downstream from the N88K mutation.

The discordant haplotype found in homozygous individuals suggests that recombination events may have occurred within the rapsyn gene and that this may have implications in the phenotypic expression of the disease.

relevance_reason: Case series of patients with congenital myasthenic syndrome caused by rapsyn (RAPSN) mutations, describing the common N88K mutation and early- and late-onset phenotypes.

findings.statement: Burke et al. (2003) identified rapsyn mutations in 16 unrelated patients with congenital/hereditary myasthenic syndrome. All of them carried the N88K mutation.
quotes: Rapsyn mutations in 16 unrelated patients with a congenital/hereditary myasthenic syndrome were identified, and a mutation (N88K) common to each of them was found.

findings.statement: Burke et al. (2003) described two distinct phenotypes in 16 unrelated patients with rapsyn-related congenital myasthenic syndrome: early onset and late onset. The early-onset form was often associated with arthrogryposis multiplex congenita and life-threatening crises. The late-onset form began in adolescence or adulthood and was at first mistaken for seronegative myasthenia gravis.
quotes: Two distinct phenotypes were noted: early and late onset. The former is frequently associated with arthrogryposis multiplex congenita and life-threatening crises.
The late-onset phenotype developed in adolescence or adulthood and was initially mistaken for seronegative myasthenia gravis.

phenotypes.text: myasthenia with onset in adolescence or adulthood

findings.statement: Burke et al. (2003) noted that recognizing the late-onset rapsyn phenotype, which can be mistaken for seronegative myasthenia gravis, should prevent inappropriate immunotherapy.
quotes: Recognition of this late-onset phenotype should prevent inappropriate immunotherapy.

relevance_reason: Reports RAPSN promoter E-box mutations in 8 patients with congenital myasthenic syndrome with predicted endplate AChR deficiency, with founder analysis and functional studies.

findings.statement: In a patient (patient 1) with congenital myasthenic syndrome, Ohno et al. (2003) identified a -27C-G mutation in the RAPSN promoter region that changes an E-box at -27 to -22 from CAGCTG to GAGCTG. The allele harboring the mutation was not transcribed in the patient's muscle. Electrophoretic mobility shift assays showed that -27C-G lost binding affinity for components of C2C12 myotube nuclear extracts, and luciferase reporter assays showed attenuated reporter expression in C2C12 myotubes and in MyoD- or myogenin-transfected HEK cells; the mutation also markedly attenuated the enhancer activity of an E-box on an SV40 promoter.
quotes: Patient 1 carries -27C-->G that changes an E-box at -27 to -22 from CAGCTG to GAGCTG. An allele harboring -27C-->G is not transcribed in patient's muscle.
-27C-->G additionally attenuates reporter gene expression in MyoD- or myogenin-transfected HEK cells
The -27C-->G mutation also markedly attenuates the enhancer activity of an E-box on an SV40 promoter.

findings.statement: Ohno et al. (2003) identified a -38A-G mutation in the RAPSN promoter in patients 2 through 8 with congenital myasthenic syndrome, all of Oriental Jewish stock of Iraqi or Iranian origin. The mutation changes an E-box at -40 to -35 from CAACTG to CAGCTG without affecting the CANNTG consensus. Electrophoretic mobility shift assays showed that -38A-G gained binding affinity for components of C2C12 myotube nuclear extracts, and luciferase reporter assays showed attenuated reporter expression in C2C12 myotubes. The authors predicted that impaired RAPSN promoter transcriptional activity would reduce rapsyn expression and cause endplate acetylcholine receptor deficiency.
quotes: Patients 2-8 are of Oriental Jewish stock of Iraqi or Iranian origin with facial malformations, and harbor -38A-->G that changes another E-box at -40 to -35 from CAACTG to CAGCTG, which does not affect the consensus CANNTG sequence.
Electrophoretic mobility shift assays reveal that -38A-->G gains, and -27C-->G looses, binding affinity for different components of nuclear extracts of C2C12 myotubes.
Impaired transcriptional activities of the RAPSN promoter region predict reduced rapsyn expression and endplate acetylcholine receptor deficiency.

findings.statement: Ohno et al. (2003) reported that the 7 congenital myasthenic syndrome patients carrying the RAPSN -38A-G promoter mutation, all Oriental Jews of Iraqi or Iranian origin, had facial malformations.
quotes: Patients 2-8 are of Oriental Jewish stock of Iraqi or Iranian origin with facial malformations

findings.statement: Haplotype analysis by Ohno et al. (2003) showed that the RAPSN -38A-G promoter mutation in Oriental Jewish patients of Iraqi or Iranian origin arose from a common founder.
quotes: Haplotype analysis shows that -38A-->G arises from a common founder.

findings.statement: Ohno et al. (2003) determined that the major transcriptional start site of RAPSN lies 172 nucleotides upstream of the translational start site.
quotes: For each mutation, position +1 represents the major transcriptional start site that we determine to be 172 nucleotides upstream of the translational start site.

relevance_reason: This paper first identified RAPSN mutations in patients with congenital myasthenic syndrome caused by endplate AChR deficiency, which is the defining paper for CMS11.

findings.statement: Ohno et al. (2002) studied 4 patients with congenital myasthenic syndrome and endplate acetylcholine receptor (AChR) deficiency who had no mutations in AChR subunit genes. In each case, endplate studies showed decreased staining for rapsyn and AChR and impaired postsynaptic morphological development.
quotes: In four patients with EP AChR deficiency but with no mutations in AChR subunits, we identify three recessive rapsyn mutations
EP studies in each case show decreased staining for rapsyn and AChR, as well as impaired postsynaptic morphological development.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormal synaptic transmission at the neuromuscular junction

phenotypes.text: impaired postsynaptic morphological development at the endplate

findings.statement: Ohno et al. (2002) identified 3 recessive RAPSN mutations in 4 patients with endplate AChR deficiency: 1 patient was compound heterozygous for L14P in TPR1 and N88K in TPR3; 2 patients were homozygous for N88K; and 1 patient was compound heterozygous for N88K and a 553ins5 frameshift in TPR5.
quotes: we identify three recessive rapsyn mutations: one patient carries L14P in TPR1 and N88K in TPR3; two are homozygous for N88K; and one carries N88K and 553ins5, which frameshifts in TPR5.

findings.statement: Ohno et al. (2002) found that the RAPSN N88K mutation, located in TPR3, was present in all 4 patients: homozygous in 2, and compound heterozygous with L14P in 1 and with 553ins5 in 1. In HEK cell expression studies, N88K did not hinder rapsyn self-association but diminished coclustering of AChR with rapsyn.
quotes: one patient carries L14P in TPR1 and N88K in TPR3; two are homozygous for N88K; and one carries N88K and 553ins5
Expression studies in HEK cells indicate that none of the mutations hinders rapsyn self-association but that all three diminish coclustering of AChR with rapsyn.

findings.statement: Ohno et al. (2002) identified a RAPSN L14P mutation in TPR1, compound heterozygous with N88K, in 1 patient with endplate AChR deficiency. In HEK cell expression studies, the mutation did not hinder rapsyn self-association but diminished coclustering of AChR with rapsyn.
quotes: one patient carries L14P in TPR1 and N88K in TPR3
Expression studies in HEK cells indicate that none of the mutations hinders rapsyn self-association but that all three diminish coclustering of AChR with rapsyn.

findings.statement: Ohno et al. (2002) identified a 5-bp insertion in RAPSN (553ins5), which causes a frameshift in TPR5, compound heterozygous with N88K, in 1 patient with endplate AChR deficiency. In HEK cell expression studies, the mutation did not hinder rapsyn self-association but diminished coclustering of AChR with rapsyn.
quotes: one carries N88K and 553ins5, which frameshifts in TPR5
Expression studies in HEK cells indicate that none of the mutations hinders rapsyn self-association but that all three diminish coclustering of AChR with rapsyn.

findings.statement: Ohno et al. (2002) noted that rapsyn is essential for clustering AChR at the endplate. Its 7 TPRs mediate self-association, a coiled-coil domain binds AChR, and a RING-H2 domain binds beta-dystroglycan. Expression studies showed that the patient mutations did not hinder rapsyn self-association but did diminish coclustering of AChR with rapsyn. This indicated that the endplate AChR deficiency results from impaired rapsyn-mediated AChR clustering.
quotes: Rapsyn, a 43-kDa postsynaptic protein, plays an essential role in the clustering of AChR at the EP.

Seven tetratricopeptide repeats (TPRs) of rapsyn subserve self-association, a coiled-coil domain binds to AChR, and a RING-H2 domain associates with beta-dystroglycan and links rapsyn to the subsynaptic cytoskeleton.
Expression studies in HEK cells indicate that none of the mutations hinders rapsyn self-association but that all three diminish coclustering of AChR with rapsyn.

findings.statement: Ohno et al. (2002) noted that many CMSs with endplate AChR deficiency had been traced to mutations in AChR subunit genes, but in a subset of patients the genetic defect had remained unknown. They found that rapsyn mutations cause some of these cases.
quotes: All CMSs with a kinetic abnormality of AChR, as well as many CMSs with a deficiency of AChR, have been traced to mutations in AChR-subunit genes. However, in a subset of patients with EP AChR deficiency, the genetic defect has remained elusive.

relevance_reason: Linkage exclusion study in Iranian Jewish families with a phenotypically unique CMS. It gives evidence for locus heterogeneity and is relevant context for the CMS11 entry.

findings.statement: Menold et al. (1998) studied 5 families of Iranian Jewish origin with 6 affected individuals who had been diagnosed with a phenotypically unique form of congenital myasthenic syndrome. Four of the families were consanguineous, and all came from the same geographic region, so the authors considered it highly likely that they carried the same ancestral CMS mutation.
quotes: We examined the DNA from 5 families of Iranian Jewish origin (6 affected individuals) who have been diagnosed with a phenotypically unique form of CMS.
Four of the families are consanguinous, and all families originate from the same geographical region, thus it is highly likely that they would carry the same ancestral CMS mutation.

findings.statement: In 5 Iranian Jewish families with CMS, Menold et al. (1998) excluded linkage to the regions on chromosomes 2 and 17 that contain the AChR subunit genes. They also excluded linkage to the chromosome 17p region to which familial infantile myasthenia had been mapped. The authors suggested that the clinical differences among patients with CMS correlate with locus heterogeneity, and that a defect in a different gene causes CMS in these patients.
quotes: We examined these families for linkage to the regions on chromosomes 2 and 17 containing the AChR subunit genes, and to the region on 17p to which FIM was localized.

Our data excludes linkage to these regions, suggesting that the clinical differences seen among patients with CMS correlate with locus heterogeneity, and that a defect in a different gene is responsible for the CMS in these patients.

relevance_reason: Review of hereditary disorders among Iranian Jews. Its abstract only says that congenital myasthenia gravis was frequent among Iranian and Iraqi Jews. It does not give the genetic subtype or any variants.

findings.statement: Zlotogora (1995) reported that congenital myasthenia gravis was among the diseases frequent in both the Iranian and Iraqi Jewish communities. Iranian Jews are an ancient community with a very high degree of inbreeding and strong ties to Babylonian Jewry in Iraq.
quotes: Other diseases, such as beta-thalassemia, achromatopsia, colobomatous microphthalmia, Dubin-Johnson syndrome, and congenital myasthenia gravis, were frequent in both the Iranian and Iraqi Jewish communities.
Iranian Jews represent an ancient community with a very high degree of inbreeding.

relevance_reason: This paper describes the clinical syndrome of congenital myasthenia with facial malformations in Iraqi and Iranian Jews, which is the CMS11 phenotype.

findings.statement: Goldhammer et al. (1990) described 14 Jewish patients from 10 families of Iraqi or Iranian origin who had congenital myasthenia with facial malformations: an elongated face, mandibular prognathism with class III malocclusion, and a high-arched palate. Muscle weakness was mostly limited to ptosis, weakness of the facial and masticatory muscles, and fatigable speech. The course was mild and nonprogressive, and patients responded to cholinesterase inhibitors.
quotes: Fourteen Jewish patients from 10 families of either Iraqi or Iranian origin with congenital myasthenia had associated facial malformations which included an elongated face, mandibular prognathism with class III malocclusion and a high-arched palate.

Other common features were muscle weakness restricted predominantly to ptosis, weakness of facial and masticatory muscles, and fatigable speech; mild and nonprogressive course; response to cholinesterase inhibitors;

findings.statement: In the patients described by Goldhammer et al. (1990), antibodies to the acetylcholine receptor were absent. Repetitive nerve stimulation at 3 Hz produced a decremental response, but a single nerve stimulus did not produce a repetitive compound muscle action potential.
quotes: absence of antibodies to acetylcholine receptor; decremental response on repetitive stimulation at 3 Hz but no repetitive compound muscle action potential in response to a single nerve stimulus.

phenotypes.text: decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation
phenotypes.hpo_label: EMG: decremental response of compound muscle action potential to repetitive nerve stimulation

findings.statement: Goldhammer et al. (1990) concluded that this newly recognized form of congenital myasthenia, which clusters by ethnicity and occurs with facial malformations, is inherited as an autosomal recessive disorder.
quotes: This newly recognized form of congenital myasthenia with distinctive ethnic clustering and associated facial malformations is transmitted as an autosomal recessive disorder.

findings.statement: Goldhammer et al. (1990) suggested that the facial abnormalities could either result from the neuromuscular defect or be primary and unrelated to it. They noted that the defect in neuromuscular transmission had yet to be identified.
quotes: The facial abnormalities may be secondary to the neuromuscular defect or may be primary and unrelated.
